title: Companion scan extras, schema 2
description: The extras object at the root of a glTF that the Companion scanner exports (schema 2, with a reader for v1 in the Companion.Spatial package). Hand written; the field names follow the web Scan contract where the concept is the same, and CONTRACT.md lists where they do not. Unknown keys are allowed everywhere on purpose: other tools and newer scanners may add them, and a reader keeps them.

schema_version.description: The schema version, a number (v1 had the text "1.0").

units.description: Every length in the file is in metres.

frames.description: The camera frames the scan kept. Always a list, empty when there are none.

objects.description: The things found in the room (v1: pins). Always a list, empty when there are none. Merged by id when a space is exported again.

planes.description: The surfaces of the headset's scene model (v1: meta_scene.anchors). Always a list, empty when there are none.

vec2.description: Two numbers on a plane's own axes, in metres.

vec3.description: A point or a size in the space's coordinate frame, in metres.

timestamp.description: An ISO 8601 time in UTC, such as 2026-11-25T10:00:00.0000000Z.

metaLabel.description: One of the 16 semantic labels of Meta's Space Setup export.

pose.description: A position and an orientation in the space's coordinate frame (the web contract's Pose, without its frame member: the frame is space.frame).

bounds.description: An axis-aligned box as a centre and a size, in metres.

box.description: A 2D box as [cx, cy, w, h], fractions of the frame image with the origin at the top left (the web contract's bbox_cxcywh).

intrinsics.description: The pinhole model of the camera for a frame, in pixels of that frame's image.

width.description: The image width in pixels; left out when unknown.

height.description: The image height in pixels; left out when unknown.

label.description: What an object is called: the text as shown, its canonical tag, and the Meta label of the tag.

text.description: The text a detector or the headset gave, as shown ("TV screen").

observation.description: One sighting of an object in a camera frame.

frame_id.description: The id of a frame in frames.

id.description: Unique in the file and stable across exports: what a re-export merges on.

track_id.description: The number of the object's track in the app run that found it; 0 when it was not tracked.

confidence.description: The fused confidence of the object (noisy-OR of its detections for a CV object, 1 for the headset's).

normal.description: The surface normal where the object was placed (a unit vector).

bounds.description: The box around the object in world space, when its extent is known.

anchor_uuid.description: The headset's anchor id, for an object from the scene model.

observations.description: The most recent sightings, oldest first. Always a list.

frame.description: One camera frame the scan kept (the web contract's keyframe).

id.description: Unique in the file and stable across exports.

image.description: The path of the JPEG beside the glTF, with forward slashes.

pose.description: Where the camera was when it took the frame.

plane.description: A surface of the headset's scene model.

label.description: The canonical tag of the plane's label ("wall").

center.description: The centre of the plane's rectangle on the plane's own x and y axes.

size.description: The size of the plane's rectangle along the plane's own x and y axes.

boundary.description: The outline of the plane in world space. Always a list, empty when the headset gave none.

id.description: The Space Setup room uuid, or "default".

frame.description: The coordinate frame of every position, rotation and size in the file: "unity-world" (metres, +Y up, left-handed) or "local-floor" (WebXR, metres, +Y up, right-handed).

consent.description: The user's agreement to the scan, recorded with the data.

notice_version.description: The version of the privacy notice the user agreed to.

server.description: The server the data may go to.

device.description: The device and the app that made the scan.
